draft.title: The problem of succession
card: Augustus held no office that could be handed down by law. He was princeps, so he could not simply name a king's heir. He had to prepare a successor in other ways.

He chose family members as heirs and gave them honours and commands. Marcellus, his nephew and son-in-law, died in 23 BC. Later Gaius and Lucius, his grandsons whom he had adopted, died in AD 2 and AD 4.
After these deaths, Augustus adopted Tiberius, his stepson, in AD 4. Tiberius was an experienced general and was already married into the family.
When Augustus died in AD 14, Tiberius took over his powers and became the next princeps. The system of one man ruling with family succession carried on.
draft.remember: Augustus had no legal way to pass on power, so he groomed family heirs, and when they died he adopted Tiberius.

a.q: Why did Augustus have to prepare his successor by adopting and promoting family members?
opts: His position as princeps could not be inherited by law
The Senate had banned him from naming any heir
He had no relatives who were old enough to rule
The title of king had passed to the consuls
a.why: Augustus ruled as princeps, a position built on powers and influence, not a legal office that passed to a son. So he used adoption and public honours to mark out an heir. The Senate did not ban him from naming heirs, and he had several relatives to choose from.
a.clue: Think about what kind of position princeps was, compared with a king.

b.q: Marcellus, then Gaius and Lucius, all died before Augustus. What did Augustus do as a result?
opts: Adopted Tiberius, his stepson, as his heir
Restored the consuls to choose a new leader
Named Agrippa Postumus, a grandson, as sole ruler
Gave up his powers and retired from public life
b.why: After the deaths of his earlier heirs, Augustus adopted Tiberius in AD 4, and Tiberius succeeded him in AD 14. He did not give up power or hand the choice back to the consuls. Tiberius was a stepson, not a grandson, so naming a grandson as sole ruler is wrong.
b.clue: Which experienced family member was adopted in AD 4?

a.best: His position as princeps could not be inherited by law

b.best: Adopted Tiberius, his stepson, as his heir

problems.detail: 'Gaius and Lucius ... died in AD 2 and AD 4' reads as respectively, but Lucius died first (AD 2) and Gaius died in AD 4. Reorder to 'Lucius and Gaius' or give each date separately.

'Tiberius ... was already married into the family' is wrong for AD 4. His marriage to Julia had ended in 2 BC, when Augustus exiled her and sent a divorce in her name. It should say he had been married to Julia.

The why's reasoning against the Agrippa Postumus option (Tiberius was a stepson, not a grandson) does not show why that option is wrong. It also hides that Augustus adopted Agrippa Postumus in AD 4 as well. The option is wrong because Postumus was not made sole ruler, and the why should say so.
The clue 'Which experienced family member was adopted in AD 4?' almost hands over the answer, since the card names Tiberius as the experienced general adopted in AD 4.

problems.detail: "his adopted grandsons Lucius ... and Gaius" is loose. They were Augustus's grandsons by birth (sons of Julia and Agrippa), whom he adopted as his sons in 17 BC. As written, a student could read it as adoption having made them his grandsons. Better: "his grandsons Lucius and Gaius, whom he had adopted as sons".
